# Registry Stack

> Open-source software for organizations building or adapting public registers and services. Base Registry Engine stores and manages records about people, households, organizations, assets, and more. It supports record creation, retrieval, relationships, controlled updates, and history, with review where required. Evidence Gateway lets approved services receive signed answers about defined facts without receiving the full source record. Each product works independently. Registry Casework assigns review requests to staff, tracks due dates, and records the decision; it returns that decision to the service that asked, which applies any change under its own rules.

Organizations own their records and define the rules for access and changes. The core software is Apache-2.0 open source. Paid pilot register implementation and annual support contracts are available for teams that need help, separate from self-service use. Current starting prices and scope are on the pricing page.

## Website

- [Home](https://registrystack.org/): Registry maintenance and fact-sharing examples, the kinds of register the software serves, product choices, and next steps.
- [Solutions](https://registrystack.org/solutions/): Organized by service area: licensing and professional registers; business, tax and finance; agriculture, animals, food and environment; people, households and social programmes; land, property, vehicles and places; health, safety and regulated products; public bodies, reference lists and catalogues. Shared capabilities cover information checks between services, staff reviews and verifiable credentials.
- [Configuration marketplace](https://marketplace.registrystack.org/): Starting configurations grouped into seven register-area collections, with their models, included parts and access requests. Current configurations are free on request and are adapted to an institution’s rules and systems. The legacy index offers collection handoffs. Detail routes remain versioned reference snapshots during migration; current configuration browsing and access requests belong in the marketplace.
- [Base Registry Engine](https://registrystack.org/products/base-registry/): Build and run the base registry other services rely on, with defined records and relationships, storage, access controls, and change history behind the organization's applications.
- [Evidence Gateway](https://registrystack.org/products/evidence-gateway/): Return signed answers from an existing registry or another configured source.
- [Registry Casework](https://registrystack.org/products/casework/): Staff review of requests that need a person to decide: queues, the officer responsible, due dates, and recorded decisions. Requests can come from a register, a case system, or another service. Registry Casework returns the decision to the service that asked and does not change the register itself. Connecting a register other than Base Registry Engine requires integration work.
- [Blog](https://registrystack.org/blog/): Field guides for registry owners and reviewers, such as defining the question before connecting a registry and reconstructing who accessed what. RSS at https://registrystack.org/rss.xml.
- [Local government](https://registrystack.org/solutions/local-government/): Local permit and registration services, from applications and staff review to record updates, notices and renewals.
- [Verifiable credentials](https://registrystack.org/solutions/verifiable-credentials/): Digital credentials that state information from a register, such as a licence's recorded status, signed so a receiving service can check who issued them and whether they were altered.
- [Digital public infrastructure](https://registrystack.org/digital-public-infrastructure/): Connect an existing source or establish a register for a programme service, using the open-source components with your own team or paid implementation and support from Aubex.
- [Data spaces](https://registrystack.org/data-spaces/): Registry Stack components an institution can use to offer or consume agreed data. The implementation connects the participant's API to the data space's chosen connector or exchange network.
- [AI for public services](https://registrystack.org/ai/): Three distinct uses: service design with partners, AI-assisted implementation with Aubex, and citizen access through an approved assistant. Each has its own review and approval. The core runtime service does not require an AI model.
- [Design a public service](https://registrystack.org/ai/service-design/): A worked method for turning research, forms and open policy questions into a reviewed service brief, illustrated with fictional school enrolment. Offered as a scoped engagement, mainly through partners.
- [Implement and adapt a service](https://registrystack.org/customization/): When we implement your pilot register, we use AI to draft configuration, test cases and guidance. The institution reviews, tests and approves each change before release. The service runs on its configured rules, with no AI model required. Registry Studio is available as a Preview.
- [AI assistants for citizen services](https://registrystack.org/ai/citizen-access/): A preview Base Registry Engine integration, outside the compatibility promise and built on Model Context Protocol (MCP), lets an assistant the institution approves help a signed-in person prepare a change to their details. The person checks and submits the draft on the institution's official website. The assistant cannot submit a request, approve it or change a record.
- [Registry Studio](https://registrystack.org/products/studio/): An authoring workspace, available as a Preview, for programme teams and implementers. It supports model review, versioned changes and document-assisted draft briefs. Contact Aubex about access. Studio has separate commercial licensing terms and is not covered by the core runtime’s Apache-2.0 licence.
- [Headless architecture](https://registrystack.org/architecture/headless/): Connect your own portal, staff interface or other software to independently deployed Registry Stack products through documented interfaces.
- [Implementation and pricing](https://registrystack.org/pricing/): Pilot register implementation, how implementation works, annual support contracts, and a written inquiry covering need, budget, and timing.
- [Security](https://registrystack.org/security/): Access, accountability, and organizational responsibilities.
- [FAQ](https://registrystack.org/faq/): Product fit, adoption, evaluation, and licensing questions.
- [About Aubex](https://registrystack.org/about/): About Aubex: the company that builds and supports Registry Stack.
- [Contact](https://registrystack.org/contact/): Ask about a registry service, implementation, support or a proposal, or request access to a starting configuration.

## Technical evaluation

- [Base Registry Engine tutorial](https://docs.registrystack.org/tutorials/first-breg/): Create and update sample records, then test a refused request.
- [Evidence Gateway tutorial](https://docs.registrystack.org/tutorials/first-evidence-assertion/): Request a signed adult-status answer from a synthetic source and verify it.
- [Registry Casework overview](https://docs.registrystack.org/start/casework/): What runs where, how work reaches the inbox from a registry or a requesting service, and which guide to open next.
- [Documentation](https://docs.registrystack.org/): Maintained tutorials, technical contracts, release status, and operational guidance.
- [Source and releases](https://github.com/registrystack/registry-stack): Public source code and released software.

Website examples illustrate possible workflows; they are not live software demonstrations.
